newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS--Oil closes lower as stocks build, coffee falls.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS--Oil closes lower as stocks build, coffee falls.

text.p: Oil prices closed lower on Tuesday as concerns about tensions with Iran faded and traders sold on expectations of rising crude oil stocks.
At the New York Mercantile Exchange, crude oil for May delivery ended seven cents a barrel lower at $19.83.
Brokers said the market felt there would be no escalation in the dispute between the European Union and Iran, the world's third largest crude exporter.

Oil prices rose on Monday partly on a weekend report in the Washington Post, attributed to U.S. and Saudi officials, linking a top Iranian official to a group suspected of the 1996 bombing of a U.S. military compound in Saudi Arabia.
That report came on the heels of a German court's ruling on Friday that Iranian leaders were behind the killing of Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
But oil brokers said they did not expect the European Union to mimic the Washington's blanket ban on trade with Tehran, focusing instead on rising crude oil supplies.
"We were overbought earlier in the session, and if we get a build in crude stocks we are bound to go lower again at the open tomorrow," said James Cordier, an analyst with Allendale Inc.
Traders had expected U.S. crude oil stocks to rise for the sixth straight week in the American Petroleum Institute's weekly report issued after the market close.
In the report, crude oil stocks rose 2.97 million barrels in the week ended April 11, against traders' expectations for a rise of 3.5 million barrels, as oil imports continued strong.

Heating oil for May delivery closed 0.18 cent a gallon higher at 54.85 cents, supported by frigid spring temperatures in much of the United States. May unleaded gasoline closed down 0.06 cent a gallon at 61.90 cents.

At the Coffee Sugar and Cocoa Exchange, coffee prices closed lower as many speculators sold on expectations that physical coffee stocks would show a big rise in a monthly report by the Green Coffee Association of New York.
Coffee for May delivery closed 3.60 cents a pound lower at 192.40 cents after trading as high as 201.50 cents early.
After the market closed, however, the association reported that supplies of green coffee housed in U.S. warehouses rose in March by only 111,000 132-pound bags to 1,657,000 bags.
Traders had been expecting an increase of 250,000 to 300,000 bags due to heavy sales this winter by producer countries rushing to cash in on higher prices.
"It is much smaller than expected," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast. "It says coffee is being absorbed rather than allowed to build stocks. The implication is bullish."
Precious metals ended sharply lower as speculators sold gold following lower-than-expected inflation data as the U.S. consumer price index for March rose only 0.1 percent.
Gold for June delivery at the Commodity Exchange ended $4.80 an ounce lower at $343.90 an ounce.
"It's a no-win situation for gold," said Bill O'Neill, Merrill Lynch's commodities research director.

"Rising real interest rates undermined the attraction of gold in the past few weeks. But when interest rates fell today in response to the inflation data, gold fell still further as low inflation also means gold is less attractive," he said.
Australian gold producers also sold gold on Tuesday, adding to the downward price pressure, analysts said.

At the Chicago Board of Trade, wheat prices fell back after Monday's strong rally as overnight cold on Tuesday was not as damaging to the young crop as the weekend freeze that clamped down on the wheat belt from Kansas to Texas.
Wheat for May delivery closed at $4.15-3/4, down 7-1/4 cents.
